references.text: God promised Moses that the people would serve Him at this mountain, which is fulfilled as the people now stand at the foot of Mount Sinai.
Israel camped before the mountain, and now Moses leads them out of the camp to meet God.
Moses reminds the people of the day they stood before the Lord at Horeb, at the foot of the mountain that burned with fire.
The Lord spoke with the people face to face on the mountain, out of the fire, and Moses stood between the Lord and the people.
Reference to the covenant the Lord made with Israel at Horeb, which was established when the people met God at the mountain.
Hebrews contrasts the Sinai experience, where the people stood before a mountain that could be touched and burned with fire, with the blessings of the new covenant.
Both verses illustrate the theology that meeting God requires separation outside the camp.
Both verses illustrate the people's holy expectation and attentiveness as Moses moves toward God's presence.
